isolation_explanation: Context isolation was isolated for the blind phase. This session did not inherit implementer chat. Requirements and failure hypotheses were recorded before diff inspection. Phase 1 was frozen and hashed before reading neutral prior closure criteria or the withheld implementer handoff. No prior audit report/verdict was read. Repository test comments naturally contained earlier finding labels. Test execution used a source copy, shared filesystem, and external cache/temp paths. The original repository was read-only by instruction, not by a separately verified OS-level write deny.

requirements.requirement: Immutable versioned acceptance contract includes run, intent, scope, non-goals, criteria IDs/statements/check/threshold/evidence, risk, deliverables, budget/route/permission ceilings. No result dispositions.
Contract criterion ID set exactly equals core run criteria; statement/check/threshold or any contract change changes digest; malformed/ambiguous bytes cannot be interpreted inconsistently.
Optional omitted acceptance_contract_digest preserves legacy approvals; required acceptance-to-planning for contract runs; later approvals carry exact contract; mismatches, drops, swaps refused.
hma.plan/v1 canonical JSON includes architecture §10 unit fields, per-unit max_wall_minutes and declared cost ceiling, required policy_digest; accepted_plan_digest binds bytes/meaning.
Plan validates unit IDs, criterion references, routes, permissions, budgets, dependencies on prior units; contract ceilings prevail; conflicts fail closed.
Lease issuer is latest approved legal unit transition to IMPLEMENTATION_AUTHORIZATION, from ROUTE_SELECTION or INDEPENDENT_VALIDATION only; no host record grants permission.
Presented validated plan must match issuer accepted_plan_digest and contain unit; legacy/no document fails closed; stable lease digest derives issuer, unit, plan.
Run nonterminal and projected unit stage IMPLEMENTATION_AUTHORIZATION; leaving stage or later relevant unit/run rewind revokes; legal rework may issue fresh lease.
Later approved dependency rewind transitively invalidates downstream leases based on approved plan; missing/invalid plan voids all.
Elapsed wall time below max_wall_minutes and counters below ceilings; per-unit grant remains within contract route, permission and budget ceilings.
Effective current policy digest equals plan policy_digest; contract digest matches approval/run; mismatch invalidates with escalation.
Existing transition, Gate B, Gate C legal edges, exact binding, invalidation, terminal coherence and review separation remain correct.
Pure derivation and model validation do not claim D3-D6 reservations, reconciliation, criterion credit, findings disposition or amendment completion.

findings.title: Required document fields can be omitted or null, including a plan that obtains an active lease
findings.diagnosis: ParsePlan accepts omitted or null budgets.max_retries as zero. ParseAcceptanceContract and ParsePlan accept absent/null check.argv. ParseAcceptanceContract accepts omitted non_goals and deliverables. The strict decoder checks duplicate/unknown keys and Unicode, but does not enforce required-key presence. Go decoding gives omitted scalar fields their zero value and omitted arrays nil; validators accept these values. A plan omitting max_retries passed ParsePlan, was bound by actual Apply transitions, was loaded from the verified store, and obtained ReasonNone from DeriveLease. This violates the required explicit plan-unit retry budget and complete acceptance/check document shape. No broader numeric grant or actual unauthorized process launch was demonstrated.

evidence.observation: Plan units must record the listed fields, including retry budgets at line 304.
Contract fields include non-goals, checks with argv, and deliverables.
validCheck iterates argv but does not reject nil.
Contract list validation checks entries, not required array presence.
MaxRetries < 0 rejects negative retries, but omitted/null becomes acceptable zero.
Independent field-removal/null tests fail on max_retries, argv, non_goals, and deliverables.
A real Apply/store chain yields an active lease from a plan without max_retries; lease digest 635cd326da24cf92bdee55a172bf302b98f6ba7c33655c96660d7bc8e0b8010e.

fix.action: Enforce required-key presence and JSON type at ParseAcceptanceContract/ParsePlan before typed decoding. Require max_retries to be a present non-null integer. Require non_goals, deliverables and every check.argv to be present arrays. Allow explicit [] where an empty list is valid, and explicit max_retries:0. Add nil-argv validation in validCheck. Preserve canonical hashing for already valid documents.
fix.why: Typed zero values cannot distinguish an explicit approved zero/empty declaration from an omitted or null field. Shape checks enforce the approved document contract before a plan can issue authority.

verification.method: Run TestAuditAllUnitFieldsDeclared and TestAuditNullRetryBudget through the supplied overlay.
verification.expected: Missing/null retry budget refused; explicit zero accepted.

verification.method: Run TestAuditExplicitCheckArgv and TestAuditContractFieldsDeclared; add explicit [] positive controls.
verification.expected: Missing/null required arrays refused; valid empty argv/non-goals arrays accepted.
The incomplete plan is refused before active lease derivation.

verification.method: Run corrected full go test, go vet, and race commands.
verification.expected: Existing stage, Gate B and Gate C behavior remains passing; accepted legacy approval bytes remain unchanged.

fix.tradeoffs: New D1/D2 document fixtures that use null required arrays must declare [] explicitly. Existing approvals must never be silently rebound: a change from null to [] changes the contract or plan digest and requires the applicable fresh human approval. A presence-only retry check preserves digests of explicit valid zero declarations.
fix.alternative: Use pointer/raw-message DTO fields during decoding, then convert to the public value structs only after checking presence and type. This is more code but keeps the existing public model unchanged.

findings.priority: Resolve before D1/D2 acceptance; independently retest the repaired document boundary.

limitations: D1/D2 only. D3-D6 reservations, durable counters, launch reconciliation, actual process enforcement, criterion credit, findings disposition and the architecture amendment are excluded.
LeaseRequest Records, counters, current policy digest and Now are trusted-host inputs. No hostile-host or authenticity claim is made.

Pure lease matrix reuses repository test fixture constructors for document/record setup; the failure reproduction uses real Apply/store calls. Independent document fixtures and tests are under this output directory.
Initial test and race runs used different GOTMPDIR and TMPDIR and failed synthetic temporary-store checks. Corrected commands align both paths and pass. The initial logs remain retained.
No approved Jev tool is exposed through the allowed host interface. No nested model API was called. Auditor decision fallback used.
Review is read-only for the target repository. Test writes and fixture Git operations occur only under the designated output directory. No user repository Git writes were performed.
Independent tests detect incomplete required fields. This is not evidence of a broader numeric permission grant or unauthorized external launch.

F01 closure includes a separate attempted-route identity mismatch check. The pure LeaseRequest has no such attempted-route input. That part was not executed or treated as fixed. Actual route use and host-attempt enforcement are D3, outside this audit.
The report-contract verdict fix-required maps to the single user verdict FAIL. It is not a second independent verdict.

This audit records the requested liz / gpt-6.1-sol / high review route from the dispatch brief. It does not independently attest model/provider execution identity. No subagent was dispatched and no nested model API or CLI was used.
No permission or stage advancement is granted by the audit or its proposed remedies.

prior_finding_closure.assessment: The in-scope plan route and permission ceilings are enforced. Outside routes and bounded_write against a read_only contract refuse. The returned lease retains the plan implementer route. The additional criterion asks for an attempted/approved-route identity mismatch while preserving the plan. LeaseRequest has no independent attempted-route/profile/permission input. No such mismatch rejection was reproduced through the current pure API. Actual requested-route enforcement is not yet wired and belongs to D3. This is an incomplete closure check, not a demonstrated D1/D2 route-identity bypass.

Direct and transitive dependency rewinds and corrections refuse. An independent unit stays active. A fresh legal issuing transition resumes the dependent with a different generation; the old issuer is not restored.

A real Apply/store case accepts an otherwise legal two-minute-old approval for a one-minute plan, then refuses its expired lease. The request just before expiry succeeds; exact expiry and time before approval refuse.

Contracts and plans reject both malformed UTF-8 byte variants and lone surrogate variants before returning a digest. Valid non-ASCII text, surrogate pairs and U+FFFD pass. Independent leaf mutations change the digest or refuse.

Most required unit fields now refuse when deleted. Missing max_retries still parses and leases; null max_retries also parses as zero. Missing/null verification argv also parses. A complete explicit plan is a passing control.

Initial presented-but-unbound contracts and wrong digests refuse. A both-absent legacy control and an exact document/digest control pass. Later and terminal transitions also reject omission or swapping.
A fresh issuer does not hide renamed, missing, extra or duplicate criterion IDs. All refuse. A disposition-only change with the same ID set remains eligible for this ID-set check.

A separately constructed JSON envelope hashed with SHA-256 equals the lease digest. The digest uses Approval.TransitionDigest, unit and plan digest. Repeated input is deterministic. Changing the record anchor alone does not change it; identity-field changes do.

Each negative signed counter refuses. Zero and below-ceiling controls pass. Equality refuses. A legal rework issuer does not erase the counters supplied by the trusted caller. Durable counter derivation is D3.
